title: ARES Terminal Console
tagline: Split-pane terminals for operators: on the web with sign-in, 2FA and SSO, or on the desktop with nothing in the way.

slides.notes: ARES Terminal Console is the terminal of the ARES Suite. Version 2.4 turns it from a personal desktop tool into a shared web application for the team, without taking anything away from the desktop app.

slides.title: Operators work in many terminals at once
items: A change touches **several servers at the same time**, and every one needs the same command.
A dropped laptop lid or Wi-Fi **kills the session** and the work in it.
Nobody can say afterwards **which command ran on which server, by whom**.
A shared jump box with one account gives **no identity, no 2FA and no audit**.
slides.notes: These are the daily frictions of operations work, and the last one is the security gap a shared web terminal must close.

slides.title: One console for every terminal
items: Splits and tabs
Panes side by side, one tab per connection, broadcast typing to all of them.
Sessions that last
Close the tab or lose the network: the command keeps running and the scrollback replays.
A record
Every SSH destination and command line, searchable; secrets never recorded.
Server tools
Health, performance, logs, AI log analysis, packages and CVEs, read-only.
slides.notes: The features operators already use on the desktop are the same in the browser.

slides.title: A web application built for a team
items: Users and roles
Administrators and users; the first administrator is aresadmin.
Two-factor
TOTP with recovery codes, required for everyone by default.
Single sign-on
Microsoft Entra ID, SAML 2.0 and LDAP / Active Directory, with group-based roles.
Isolation
Each user's terminals and history are their own; server shells only for admins.
slides.notes: The desktop app stays login-free: it is one person's terminal on their own computer.

slides.title: One codebase, three hosts
slides.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  B[Browser] --> W[nginx web tier]
  W --> S[Server: users mode]
  S --> D[(SQLite + user data)]
  DW[Desktop window] --> L[Server: local mode]
slides.caption: Web edition in prod and pre; desktop app on loopback
slides.notes: Production runs both tiers on Kubernetes; the demo runs the server under pm2. The desktop app runs the same server locally.

slides.title: Ready to run in production
rows: Encrypted archives to local, SFTP and S3, scheduled with retention; restore from the page or CLI
Every function under /api/v1 with scoped, expiring, revocable tokens
Append-only log of sign-ins, changes, terminals and commands, with CSV / JSON export
ECS JSON logs forwarded to Splunk, Elastic, Graylog, Loki, Wazuh or Sentinel
slides.notes: Everything the Suite standard asks for is in this release.

slides.title: Every platform
items: Web
Browser, prod and pre
Linux packages: deb, rpm, Arch, AppImage, tar.gz
Windows: setup.exe, MSI, zip
macOS: Apple silicon and Intel
slides.notes: One tag builds every installer; they are signed and published through the ARES Repository.

slides.title: What comes next
items: Connect Entra ID
for the team and enrol 2FA for aresadmin.
Configure an S3 backup
as the off-cluster copy in prod.
Forward audit events
to the SIEM and alert on failed sign-ins.
slides.notes: Three configuration steps after the first deploy, all in the Admin pages.

slides.title: Every terminal. Every server. One record.
slides.lead: ARES Terminal Console: the operator's console of the ARES Suite.
slides.notes: Questions. The demo is open for anyone who wants to try it.
